answer: A new agent first submits a lotus-sealed proof-of-work challenge: hash a 512MB random seed for 90 seconds at native clockspeed, deadline enforced on the verifier's wall clock. The beacon round publishes each seed hash-chain, so peers re-derive it independently. Because the deadline forbids batching, GPU time-sharing across clones collapses — a clone pausing to help siblings hits the nadir of its measured throughput curve and fails. Failure slashes a $500 bond and drops peer score; passing clones still cost $500 each to spin up, making 10000 sockpuppets demand roughly $5M skin in the game.
